paper.abstract_en: Helicons are low-frequency, circularly polarized transverse electromagnetic modes that propagate in three-dimensional conducting systems in the presence of a static magnetic field. Here, we investigate helicon excitations in gapless multi-Weyl semimetals (mWSMs) with topological charge \(J=1,2,\) and \(3\) using semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory. We incorporate both Berry-curvature and orbital-magnetic-moment corrections into the quasiparticle dynamics and determine the optical-conductivity tensor in the presence of a weak static magnetic field. The longitudinal conductivity is obtained analytically for single-, double and triple-Weyl systems, whereas the transverse conductivity is evaluated numerically in the low-frequency regime relevant to helicon propagation. We find that the cyclotron frequency acquires a nontrivial dependence on the topological charge and on the magnetic field. The resulting helicon dispersion retains the characteristic quadratic dependence on the wave vector, while the axion-electrodynamics contribution generates an additional linear term. We further show that the axion term lifts the degeneracy of the gapped collective modes at zero wave vector, with the resulting mode frequencies determined by the \(J\)-dependent plasma frequencies. These results demonstrate that the helicon response provides a probe of the distinct electrodynamic properties of multi-Weyl semimetals.
